featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
The history of this club is interesting, but its current policy is total nonsense. This club is strictly meant only for life members and their descendants. While I personally have no involvement with this, they should at least mention this crucial fact on their website.
​I recently moved from Sion to Tardeo, and after searching online, I visited this club today as it was the nearest swimming pool. However, the watchman informed me that membership is strictly hereditary, intended only for blood relatives. He also stated that no new memberships have been granted since 1995.
​This situation is truly disgusting because they fail to mention this restriction online. I assume that countless people must have visited over the years, only to leave disappointed. This current owner/s' mentality is extremely poor—it's a form of harassment for non-members, perhaps seeking publicity or some perverse pleasure.
​If that is not the case, they must immediately update their website with this fact. Doing so would prevent the wastage of time and harassment of non-members.

featured_reviews.review_text: Clean and well maintained facility, very helpful staff's,  always alert lifeguard's, very professional, knowledgeable, encouraging, motivating and most importantly very understanding coaches and a highly alert head coach with an eagle's eye on every student and coach. Swimming lessons are given in a very professional manner keeping in mind every student's comfort level in water. Like to thank Coach Navdeep for understanding my spine disc buldge, severe Sciatica pain and water phobia issue and training me accordingly starting with simple water exercise. I would like to thank coach Rohit sir too for switching me to breaststroke swimming keeping in mind my repetitive Spine, Sciatica pain and leg cramps issues. featured_reviews.name: Irfan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I joined the swimming program at Michael Phelps Swimming India, Kohinoor Club Kurla, expecting a professional and hygienic environment, but unfortunately my experience was disappointing.

The biggest concern is cleanliness and hygiene. The washroom areas are not maintained properly and often feel unhygienic. The pool maintenance also needs serious improvement. Additionally, there is no proper shade or sun protection around the pool area, making it uncomfortable during peak daytime sessions.

Another issue is the lack of proper team management and professionalism among some staff members. There seems to be poor coordination between coaches, and arguments or conflicts happening in front of students create an uncomfortable environment. Some coaches also appear uninterested and non-cooperative during sessions, which affects the overall learning experience.

There were also occasions where staff members appeared to consume tobacco products before or during sessions, which created an unpleasant environment due to strong odor and felt highly unprofessional around students and parents.

Communication is another challenge due to language barriers, and overall the atmosphere feels poorly managed for a place that represents such a reputed name.

I hope the management takes these concerns seriously and improves the hygiene, professionalism, discipline, and overall experience for students and parents.

He pays attention to every detail and helps you overcome your fears in the water. Each session is fun, challenging, and confidence-boosting. Highly recommend him to anyone wanting to improve their swimming skills!

featured_reviews.review_text: My daughter who is 3 yrs old was enrolled at the pre beginner level 3 months ago, after 21 sessions the staff got completely changed and the students nor the parents were told of this situation. Now the new teachers are teaching again from the basics instead of taking the child's progress ahead. There is no head coach to talk to nor does the head office reply to the emails. I do not recommend this franchise of Micheal Phelps Swimming to anybody.

featured_reviews.name: Supreme Kothari
featured_reviews.review_text:
The idea of personal coaching during a 40-minute session here seems to run entirely on luck—and unfortunately, luck doesn’t favor everyone every day. Like today, for instance—my daughter got a few seconds of attention right at the end, while the coach’s focus remained firmly on a younger child throughout. Maybe there’s a secret lottery system? If so, we’d love to know how to sign up.

Also, during rains (like on 1st June), it’s perfectly normal here for most coaches to simply step out while kids are left to figure things out on their own. Because, of course, why would Michael Phelps’ name imply any higher standard, especially in India?

And yes, batch change chaos is part of life—we get that. But if it regularly eats into actual swimming time, then it stops being "chaos" and starts becoming bad planning.

If there’s some unofficial premium fee that buys actual attention, please do let us know. We'd be happy to pay, instead of just crossing our fingers each time.

We expected the name to come with certain standards. Right now, it feels more like a branding exercise than a coaching one.

featured_reviews.name: kiran karande
featured_reviews.review_text:
“Michael Phelps Swimming Academy at Universal Chembur is an absolute gem for anyone looking to dive into the world of swimming, from beginners to advanced swimmers alike. The facility is meticulously maintained, offering a clean, hygienic environment that’s immediately welcoming and sets the tone for a safe and enjoyable swimming experience. The pool itself is beautifully designed and well-equipped, making it ideal for swimmers of all levels.

The coaching staff is truly top-notch, with well-trained instructors who bring patience, expertise, and personalized attention to each swimmer. The academy follows the Michael Phelps method, ensuring that techniques are taught correctly with a strong focus on form and safety. The coaches are approachable, motivating, and skilled in working with everyone from young children to adults, adapting their approach based on the needs and skill levels of each participant. For those who might be a bit nervous or lack confidence in the water, the coaches are fantastic at building trust and helping swimmers gradually overcome their fears.

The pool’s water quality is exceptional, as it is regularly tested and maintained, ensuring a pleasant swimming experience without the overpowering smell of chlorine that some pools can have. The entire space, from the pool to the changing areas, is kept extremely clean, adding to the sense of professionalism and care that the facility offers.

The management at Universal Chembur has clearly invested in creating a high-quality swimming experience. They provide all necessary amenities, and there’s a strong emphasis on safety, with lifeguards always on duty and clear guidelines for both swimmers and spectators. The academy also offers convenient scheduling options, so whether you’re looking for early morning sessions or evening classes, there’s something to fit a variety of schedules.

featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
My recent visit to Nahar's Nectarfield clubhouse left me with mixed feelings. On one hand, the clubhouse boasts an impressive array of facilities, including a stunning swimming pool, baby pool, basketball and tennis courts, badminton facilities, a well-equipped gym, a salon, and spacious banquet halls, all thoughtfully designed and meticulously maintained. The physical infrastructure is undoubtedly commendable.

However, the shining exterior contrasts starkly with the glaring shortcomings of the staff. It's regrettable to report that the staff's performance was far from satisfactory. Their conduct lacked basic courtesy, and interactions with them were often uncomfortable. Furthermore, their knowledge of the clubhouse's rules and regulations left much to be desired, resulting in frequent confusion and frustration among visitors and members alike. It seemed that the staff had no clue about the rules, and every member seemed to receive different information, creating a perplexing and chaotic atmosphere.

What was perhaps most disappointing was the staff's apparent lack of empathy. They seemed disinterested in addressing concerns or providing assistance, failing to create the warm and welcoming atmosphere one would expect at a club of this caliber.

It was also disheartening to note that regardless of whether one was a guest, a member, or a child, the staff's level of service remained consistently lacking. This lack of differentiation in service levels was a glaring issue.

Furthermore, the pricing structure at Nahar's Nectarfield raised eyebrows. The fees, even for residents of Nahar's Amrit Shakti, appeared unjustifiably high. Guest charges, in particular, bordered on the exorbitant, making it less accessible for those wishing to enjoy the facilities on occasion.

Lastly, the on-site restaurant, while aesthetically pleasing, left much to be desired in terms of service and food quality. Surprisingly, it did not cater to non-vegetarian preferences, even though members are non-vegetarian enthusiasts.

In conclusion, Nahar's Nectarfield clubhouse presents an impressive array of amenities and infrastructure. However, the staff's professionalism, or rather the lack thereof, and their inability to provide clear, consistent information regarding rules and policies, cast a shadow over the overall experience. Urgent improvements in staff training, people skills, and customer service are essential to bring this otherwise promising establishment up to par with its potential. Additionally, a reevaluation of pricing and an enhancement of the restaurant's offerings would further contribute to making Nahar's Nectarfield a truly exceptional destination for its members and guests.
